I THOUGHT IT WAS IMPORTANT THAT WE RECOGNIZE THAT IN THE CITY OF TAMPA, WE HAVE A LOT OF HIDDEN FIGURES. ONE OF THOSE, MADAM CHAIR, IS DR. BERNARD LAFAYETTE. AS MR. DOSS CALLED IN AND TALKED ABOUT EARLIER TODAY, HE'S NOT SOMEBODY I FEEL THE CITY SHOULD RECOGNIZE BECAUSE HE LIVED HERE, BUT WE SHOULD RECOGNIZE HIM BECAUSE HE BECAME A PART OF THE HISTORY OF THE ENTIRE COUNTRY. COUPLE OF WEEKS I WAS AT THE CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS MEETINGS IN WASHINGTON, D.C., AND HE WAS RECOGNIZED AT THE HIGHEST LEVELS IN OUR NATION'S CAPITOL. I FEEL THAT TAMPA SHOULD BE DOING THE SAME THING FOR A MAN OF HIS STATURE. THOSE NOT FAMILIAR WITH DR. LAFAYETTE, HE WAS BORN AND RAISED IN TAMPA IN 1940. HE WENT FROM THE STREETS OF THE CITY TO THE FRONT LINES OF THE AMERICAN CIVIL RIGHTS MOVEMENT. HE BECAME A FREEDOM RIDER, A FOUNDING LEADER OF THE STUDENT NONVIOLENT COORDINATING COMMITTEE, AN ORGANIZER OF THE SELMA VOTING RIGHTS CAMPAIGN, AND LATER A TRUSTED MEMBER OF MARTIN LUTHER KING'S SOUTHERN CHRISTIAN LEADERSHIP CONFERENCE. HIS ENTIRE LIFE'S WORK HELPED TO SHAPE THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA. BUT THE REASON WHY TAMPA HAS A SPECIAL CLAIM TO HIS STORY IS THAT THE SEEDS OF HIS EXTRAORDINARY LIFE WERE PLANTED RIGHT HERE IN TAMPA. DR. LAFAYETTE OFTEN RECOUNTED BEING SEVEN YEARS OLD AND RIDING IN A SEGREGATED STREETCAR WITH HIS GRANDMOTHER. BLACK PASSENGERS WERE REQUIRED TO PAY IN THE FRONT AND THEN WALK AROUND AND ENTER THROUGH THE REAR. ON ONE OCCASION, AFTER HIS GRANDMOTHER PAID THE FARE, THE STREETCAR PULLED AWAY AS THEY ATTEMPTED TO BOARD, KNOCKING HER TO THE GROUND. DR. LAFAYETTE WOULD DESCRIBE THAT EXPERIENCE AND THE HELPLESSNESS THAT HE FELT WHILE WATCHING THIS AS ONE OF THE EXPERIENCES THAT CONVINCED HIM THAT SOMETHING HAD TO CHANGE. IN OTHER WORDS, ONE OF AMERICA'S GREAT APOSTLES OF NONVIOLENCE FIRST CONFRONTED THE INJUSTICE HE WOULD SPEND HIS LIFE FIGHTING RIGHT HERE IN TAMPA. HE LEFT TAMPA AS A YOUNG MAN FOR NASHVILLE WHERE HE STUDIED NONVIOLENCE ALONG WITH JOHN LEWIS, DIANE NASH, AND OTHER STUDENTS WHO WOULD GULF COAST GIANTS OF THE CIVIL RIGHTS MOVEMENT. HE PARTICIPATED IN THE NATIONAL SIT-INS AND FREEDOM RIDES AND AT ONLY 22 YEARS OLD WAS SENT TO SELMA, ALABAMA, TO ORGANIZE BLACK VOTER REGISTRATION. THE ORGANIZING INFRASTRUCTURE HE HELPED TO ESTABLISH THERE BECAME PART OF THE FOUNDATION FOR THE SELMA MOVEMENT THAT CULMINATED IN THE VOTING RIGHTS ACT OF 1965. DR. KING LATER SELECTED LAFAYETTE TO SERVE AS PROGRAM DIRECTOR OF THE SCLC AND DR. LAFAYETTE MET WITH DR. KING ON THE MORNING OF APRIL 4, 1968, A DAY THAT WILL LIVE IN INFAMY IN THIS COUNTRY BECAUSE IT WAS THE DAY THAT DR. KING WAS ASSASSINATED. TAMPA HAS A LOT OF STREETS AND MONUMENTS NAMED AFTER PEOPLE TO PRESERVE THE HISTORY AND THE EVENTS THAT HAVE HAPPENED HERE SO WE CAN TELL OUR STORY AS A CITY. DR. BERNARD LAFAYETTE BELONGS IN THAT STORY. NOT JUST BECAUSE TAMPA WAS WHERE HE WAS BORN, BUT BECAUSE THE EXPERIENCES HE HAD HERE IN TAMPA HELPED SHAPE THE SAME CONVICTION THAT HE TOOK ON TO BUSES, TO LUNCH COUNTER DEMONSTRATIONS THROUGH SELMA AND ULTIMATELY AROUND THE WORLD AS A TEACHER OF NONVIOLENCE. I DON'T KNOW WHAT YOU ALL SHOULD DO, BUT I WILL SAY THAT A STREET, A PLAZA, A PERMANENT BUST ON THE RIVERWALK, SOMETHING BEARING HIS NAME AND LIKENESS WOULD THEREFORE DO MORE THAN JUST HONOR ONE MAN, AS MR. DOSS CALLED IN AND SAID, IT WOULD TEACH FUTURE GENERATIONS THAT TAMPA PRODUCED ONE OF THE ARCHITECTS OF THE MODERN CIVIL RIGHTS MOVEMENT. CHILDREN GROWING UP HERE, THEY NEED TO KNOW THAT SOMEONE WHO WALKED THE SAME STREETS THAT THEY DID ULTIMATELY HELPED CHANGE THE COURSE OF AMERICA. PRESERVING THAT HISTORY THAT'S GOING TO HELP CONNECT TAMPA'S PAST TO ITS PRESENT AND ENSURE THAT DR. LAFAYETTE'S REMARKABLE JOURNEY FROM A CHILD CONFRONTING RACISM ON THE STREETS OF TAMPA TO A LEADER WHO HELPED TRANSFORM AMERICA IS NEVER FORGOTTEN. AGAIN, AS I STARTED OUT, WE HAVE A WONDERFUL HISTORY IN THIS CITY. I THINK A HIDDEN HISTORY. I'VE BEEN HERE 32 YEARS AND LEARNED SOMETHING NEW ABOUT THE FIGURES, WE HAVE REMARKABLE PLAQUES AND PLACARDS TO ALL THE TIME. HERE IS A CHANCE FOR THIS COUNCIL TO HONOR ONE OF OUR OWN. SO, YEAH, THAT'S WHAT I'D LOVE TO SEE. WHAT I WOULD SUGGEST -- THIS IS MY LAST CRA MEETING, RIGHT? MADAM CHAIR, IF SOMEBODY CAN HAVE ELECTED JURISDICTION OVER IT, SO IT'S NOT MY MOTION. segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: GO BULLS. I DID A LOT OF WORK WITH STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND CIVIC ENGAGEMENT AS WELL AS STUDYING RESTORATION OF VOTING RIGHTS WITH RETURNING CITIZENS. I'M CURRENTLY APPLYING FOR LAW SCHOOLS. I HOPE TO BECOME AN ATTORNEY. [ APPLAUSE ]

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: MARISSA JUST STARTED WITH US ON TUESDAY. SHE HAS ALREADY HIT THE GROUND RUNNING. WE ARE VERY HAPPY TO HAVE HER IN THE OFFICE AND GETTING ALL THE EXPERIENCE. SO WELCOME. I ALSO HAVE A MOTION. RECENTLY, WHAT WE HAVE DISCOVERED, WE KNOW THAT WE HAVE THE HOUSING REHABILITATION RENOVATION PROGRAM. AND THERE ARE FEW HOMES, PARTICULARLY I KNOW IN EAST TAMPA, THEY ARE A LITTLE BIT OLDER THAN OTHERS. SO RIGHT NOW THE AMOUNT IS CANNOT GO ABOVE THE 150,000. I'VE BEEN WORKING WITH OUR CRA DIRECTOR AND STAFF AND ATTORNEY SHEPARD TO CRAFT THIS MOTION. I'LL SAY IT AND SEE HOW IT GOES. THE MOTION IS REQUESTING THE HOUSING REHABILITATION AND RENOVATION PROGRAM WITH THE CURRENT STANDARD MAXIMUM PROJECT ASSISTANCE AMOUNT OF 150,000 PER ELIGIBLE PROPERTY TO AUTHORIZE THE CRA DIRECTOR TO APPROVE HR PROJECTS EXCEEDING 150,000 UP TO A MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF 200,000 ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS WHEN THERE ARE DOCUMENTED EXTREME OR EXCEPTIONAL CIRCUMSTANCES EXISTING OR OVERALL LIFE, SAFETY OR HABITABILITY CONCERNS, INCLUDING PROJECTS LOCATED INSIDE ANY APPLICABLE OVERLAY DISTRICT ESTABLISHED WITHIN THE CRA AREAS.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: SECOND.

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: THIS WILL BE FOR ANY NEW APPLICATIONS THAT WE GET. IT WOULDN'T BE RETROACTIVE. WE'VE BEEN SEEING THERE ARE A FEW HOUSES THAT ARE A LITTLE BIT OLDER AND THAT AMOUNT IS NOT COVERING EVERYTHING. FOR FUTURE APPLICATIONS COMING IN, WANTED TO PUT THAT INTO CONSIDERATION. I KNOW I TALKED WITH DIRECTOR McCRAY, IS THERE ANYTHING YOU WANT TO ADD THAT I DIDN'T EXPLAIN WELL?

segments.speaker: CEDRIC McCRAY
segments.text: NO. MS. PARKS IS HERE. SHE'S UNDER THE WEATHER THIS MORNING. I DID SHARE SOME OF THE CONVERSATION WE HAD YESTERDAY WITH HER.
